title: P0 hosted API - ACK window starvation postmortem
content:
Summary:

On 2029-12-18 between ~02:12 and ~03:05 UTC we experienced a P0 degradation of hosted API streaming sessions resulting in elevated TTFB and partial session stalls for approximately 11% of active streaming connections in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. User-visible symptoms included long pauses between data chunks, reconnects, and ~5–8% increase in 5xx errors for streaming endpoints (non-chat gen endpoints were mostly unaffected).

This incident was caused by an ACK window starvation condition introduced by a recent edge batching change (PR #2847) that interacted poorly with cross-region KV lease invalidation. A small timer drift and an ordering bug in the streaming multiplexer allowed backpressure counters to block the ACK path for certain client session shapes, preventing the reassembly/flush of buffered chunk frames until a lease refresh or client retransmit.

Impact:
- Time window: 2029-12-18 02:12–03:05 UTC (partial recovery started at 02:38 after emergency mitigations; final rollback completed 03:05).
- Affected customers: ~11% of streaming sessions routed through eu-west-1/eu-central-1 edges (approx. 1.2k sessions at peak).
- User-visible effects: increased TTFB on streaming responses, intermittent chunk gaps, higher reconnect rate, transient 5xx rate bump (~5–8% for streaming APIs).
- Business: short-lived but P0 severity due to latency SLO violations and customer reports. No data loss observed.

Timeline (reconstructed from traces/logs & pager notes):
- 02:07 UTC: deploy of serving-runtime PR #2847 (edge egress batching improvements) started to two canaries and then staged to eu-west-1.
- 02:12 UTC: SRE oncall alert: p95 TTFB streaming > alert threshold for eu-west-1. Pager page sent to eng-sre.
- 02:15 UTC: Oncall connects to runbook, runs quick perf queries; notices elevated ack-latency and backlog on multiplexer metrics (ack_window_wait_count).
- 02:18 UTC: First mitigation: increase ack-window timeout threshold on edge config (hotpatch) — partial improvement but not resolved.
- 02:25 UTC: Hypothesis shifts to batching interaction — rollback of new batching config to canaries initiated.
- 02:33 UTC: Canary rollback shows symptom regression but still present for sessions with cross-region KV lease churn.
- 02:38 UTC: Emergency full-region rollback of PR #2847 to previous egress behavior begins. Incremental recovery in metrics observed.
- 03:05 UTC: Rollback completes; streaming p95/p99 back within SLOs. Post-incident monitoring continues.

Detection and Response Notes (on-call POV):
- Detection was via existing p95/p99 TTFB alerts for streaming. Alert thresholds fired correctly.
- Investigation leveraged real-time trace watermarks (trace ids in alert emails were helpful), multiplexer counters, and KV lease churn events from the control plane.
- Early confusion: initial signals suggested network flakiness; packet-level telemetry showed healthy connectivity. The primary signal was ack_window_wait_count and a new backpressure histogram that had just been added with the batching change.
- Communication: initial customer-facing Slack post at 02:22 UTC, status page incident opened at 02:28 UTC. We escalated to Platform & Serving Runtime immediately.

Root cause analysis:
Primary root cause (technical):
- The edge egress batching PR changed scheduling to prefer larger batches and introduced an optimistic path that deferred ACK propagation until a batch-flush event. A rare timing window, combined with a timer drift on certain edge hosts and a race in the streaming multiplexer, meant that the ACK propagation code could be skipped for sessions waiting on a pending KV lease refresh. When the control-plane invalidated/rotated KV leases for routing (cross-region failover path), those sessions entered a state where the multiplexer held onto buffers and the ACK window counter saturated, starving ACKs to the client and preventing the session from making forward progress.

Contributing factors: 
- New batching telemetry lacked an explicit ack-latency dimension at p99; we did not have a direct alert for ack-starvation.
- KV lease churn (control-plane churn) due to a minor reconcilation cycle overlapped with the rollout; spikes in lease-invalidations were not correlated in dashboards we normally inspected.
- The multiplexer had a subtle ordering bug: under rare interleavings the ack-path was gated by a backpressure counter that assumed flush would be triggered by the same timer that the batching change replaced. This was not covered by existing unit tests.
- Canary rollout scope was insufficient for cross-region lease patterns; canaries were predominantly in a single region and did not exercise cross-region control-plane events.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Reverted the batching change across affected edges (completed by 03:05 UTC).
- Hotpatched ack-window timeout to be more permissive (temporary) to allow sessions to clear buffered frames while rollback propagated.
- Increased the sampling rate for streaming traces to capture pre/post rollback behavior for root cause confirmation.

Long-term remediation plan (concrete action items):
- Fix the multiplexer ordering bug and add deterministic concurrency tests. Owner: Diego Martinez. ETA: 2029-12-30.
- Rework batching implementation to always expose an ACK-forwarding fast-path when ack_window_wait_count grows. Owner: Serving Runtime team (Diego). ETA: 2029-12-27.
- Add a dedicated alert and dashboard for ack_window_p99 and ack_window_wait_count with regional breakdown and cross-region lease-churn correlation. Owner: Maya Singh (observability). ETA: 2029-12-24.
- Add integration test that simulates KV lease churn during batch flushes and validates no ack starvation. Owner: Sofia Patel (platform-engineering tests). ETA: 2029-12-28.
- Expand canary rollout policy to include cross-region lease churn scenarios and add synthetic traffic patterns that emulate long-tail session shapes. Owner: Release Engineering. ETA: 2029-12-22.
- Postmortem follow-up doc + conformance checklist for future batching changes (include runbook-check items). Owner: Avery Chen. ETA: 2029-12-23.

Runbook changes (what to add/update):
- New runbook step: if streaming p95/p99 increases without network anomalies, check ack_window_wait_count and ack_window_p99 first.
- Add a quick mitigation to temporarily relax ack-window gating and fall back to non-batched path if ack-window waits exceed threshold for 5 minutes.
- Add playbook to correlate KV lease churn (control plane) with streaming metrics and run pre-flight checks for rolling restarts.

Monitoring and metrics adjustments:
- Create streaming:ack_window_p99 (region, model, tenant dimensions).
- Create streaming:ack_window_wait_count alarm (alert when > 1000 events in 5m for region).
- Add a synthetic canary that exercises small-chunk streaming paths with lease-rotation induced events periodically.

Post-incident customer communication plan:
- Draft a concise summary for the status page covering root cause and that a rollback mitigated the issue; include ETA for long-term fixes. Owner: Customer Success. ETA: 2029-12-20.
- Offer outreach to top 10 affected customers with technical notes and mitigation guidance. Owner: Solutions Engineering. ETA: 2029-12-21.

Lessons learned (high level):
- Any change that reorders or defers network-visible signals (ACKs) must include clear telemetry and an auditable fast-path.
- Canary coverage must include cross-region control-plane events and not just single-region traffic shapes.
- Small timer drifts and race windows in multiplexer/edge code can have outsized user impact; invest in deterministic concurrency tests.

Action item table (short):
- Diego Martinez: Fix multiplexer ordering + tests — due 2029-12-30.
- Diego Martinez / Serving Runtime: Rework batching ack fast-path — due 2029-12-27.
- Maya Singh: New ack_window metrics + alerts — due 2029-12-24.
- Sofia Patel: Integration test for lease-churn + batching — due 2029-12-28.
- Release Eng: Canary policy change & synthetic traffic — due 2029-12-22.
- Avery Chen: Postmortem finalization and runbook checklist — due 2029-12-23.
- Customer Success / Solutions Eng: Customer comms and outreach — due 2029-12-21.

Appendix (logs, quick commands, links):
- Relevant traces: trace ids included in linked_artifacts (confluence page).
- Quick diagnostics commands used oncall:
  - kubectl -n edge logs --since=10m --selector=app=edge-mux | grep ack_window
  - curl -sS https://internal-metrics/streaming/ack_window_p99?region=eu-west-1
  - /scripts/hotpatch/edge-set-config.sh --set ack_window_timeout=1200 --region eu-west-1

Notes to self / open questions (for follow-up):
- Why did canary in the other region not show symptoms earlier? Need to validate canary traffic diversity and confirm that canaries were not pinned to hosts with stable timers.
- Confirm if any tenant-specific session shapes (large initial prompt + sparse followups) are more vulnerable — add tenant-dimension to new metrics.
- Investigate whether KV lease reconciliation cadence needs smoothing across control-plane to avoid simultaneous churn during rollouts.

Status: in_review.
